s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on the trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on the lower lip with sparing of the surrounding skin
key_facts: Topical corticosteroids did not control symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis, erosions, and nodular lymphocyte infiltrate
Phototest with solar simulator showed delayed erythema to UV-A

raw.rationale: The presence of erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations, along with scales and fissures on the lower lip, and the skin biopsy showing spongiosis, erosions, and nodular lymphocyte infiltrate, are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus. The normal blood test results, including antinuclear antibodies, and the lack of other systemic symptoms also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While the skin biopsy shows a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate, the presence of germinal centers and the clinical presentation are more consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus. Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma typically presents with more aggressive and widespread lesions.
